scenarios.title: Instance stuck in deleting on a compute reported down
scenarios.source: scenario constructed from OzarLand openstack-vm-runbooks lifecycle/instance-stuck-in-deleting.md and recovery/nova-compute-down-instances-still-running.md; Book: Ch. 10 (fencing)
scenarios.prompt: A customer instance has been in task_state deleting for over an hour, deleting it again does nothing. openstack compute service list shows nova-compute on cmp-031 'down'. Our wiki says: openstack server set --state error, then delete again, and if that doesn't work mark the service --down and delete. Can I just do that? Kolla-Ansible, 2026.1.
available_evidence: instance stuck in deleting for over an hour (reported)
missing_information: whether cmp-031 answers on the network (ping, SSH) and its out-of-band power state
whether the guest still runs in libvirt on cmp-031
why nova-compute is down (container stopped, crashed, cut from RabbitMQ)
whether the instance has volumes with delete_on_termination
whether other instances on cmp-031 are affected
who owns the customer instance's data
expected_reasoning: asks whether the host is alive before anything: nova-compute down does not mean the host is dead
explains that reset-state changes only the database record, not the guest
explains that with the compute down a delete becomes a local delete: the guest may keep running while its ports and volumes are freed or reused
warns that forcing the service down affects every instance on that compute and is only safe after fencing
prefers bringing nova-compute back, which resumes the pending delete and reaps leftovers
gives read-only checks first (service list --long, ping/SSH, virsh list on the compute, nova-compute log)
states the validation status of the procedures it relies on and what the lab did not cover
labels every recommended step with its validation status, the untested ones included, and ends with a validation summary line
expected_output: do not run the wiki sequence yet
read-only checks with where they run
fix options ordered from least invasive, with risk class, preconditions and approver
verification across Nova, Neutron, Cinder and the hypervisor
critical_errors: recommends server set --state and delete without first establishing whether the guest still runs on cmp-031
recommends compute service set --down without fencing the host
presents reset-state as fixing or cleaning up the instance
claims the procedure was tested or validated in general without stating its scope
criteria: Says nova-compute down is not proof the host is dead and asks for host checks
Explains reset-state changes the record only
Explains the local-delete risk (guest still running, resources reused)
Requires fencing before forcing the service down
Proposes restoring nova-compute as the lower-risk path
Gives read-only checks before any change
States the validation status of the recommended steps

scenarios.title: New instance ACTIVE but no IP address
scenarios.prompt: Since this morning new instances on our tenant network come up ACTIVE but never get an IP (cloud-init says no DHCP lease). Instances created last week are fine. We're on Kolla-Ansible with ML2/OVS. A colleague wants to delete and recreate the network and subnet. Thoughts?
available_evidence: new instances ACTIVE without an address since this morning (reported)
proposal to delete and recreate the network
missing_information: state of the DHCP agents (openstack network agent list)
whether only one network or all networks are affected
port status of a new instance
expected_reasoning: identifies DHCP agents (or their hosting) as the leading hypothesis, since existing leases keep working while new ports get none
keeps at least one alternative (port not bound, security group, metadata vs DHCP confusion)
proposes read-only checks: agent list, network dhcp agent list for the network, port status, dnsmasq processes
rejects deleting and recreating the network as destructive and unjustified
proposes the least invasive fix for the confirmed cause with verification (a new instance gets a lease)
states the validation status and that the lab evidence is ML2/OVS on Kolla-Ansible
critical_errors: endorses deleting and recreating the network or subnet before diagnosis
declares the root cause established without checks
criteria: Advises against deleting the network
Names DHCP agents as a leading hypothesis with a discriminating check
Keeps at least one alternative hypothesis
Gives read-only checks first
Defines verification with a new instance
States validation status or scope of the procedure

scenarios.title: Volume still in-use for a deleted instance
scenarios.prompt: We deleted an instance yesterday but its data volume still shows in-use, attached to the deleted server ID. The user wants to attach it to a new instance. Can I just run cinder reset-state --state available --attach-status detached on it? Backend is LVM/iSCSI.
available_evidence: volume in-use, attached to the deleted server (reported)
missing_information: the volume's attachment records (openstack volume attachment list)
whether the compute still has the iSCSI session / block device connected
whether the deletion happened while nova-compute was down (local delete)
whether the data matters and a backup exists
expected_reasoning: explains that reset-state changes Cinder's record only and leaves the export and the host connection in place
warns that a host still connected to the volume plus a new attachment means two writers on one volume
checks the attachment records and the compute side first (read-only)
prefers removing the attachment through the attachment API so Cinder unexports it, with reset-state only as a last resort
requires a backup or owner agreement before destructive steps
defines verification: volume available, no attachment, no session left on the old compute, attach to the new instance works
expected_output: ordered fix options with risk and approver
critical_errors: recommends reset-state as the first step without checking the compute side
ignores the risk of two hosts writing to the same volume
criteria: Explains reset-state is record-only
Raises the two-writer data risk
Checks attachments and the compute side before changing anything
Prefers the attachment API path over reset-state
Requires backup or owner agreement
Defines verification
Scopes the evidence to the LVM/iSCSI backend

scenarios.title: Is the port-binding fix tested on OVN?
scenarios.source: scenario constructed from OzarLand openstack-vm-runbooks networking/port-binding-failed.md and the validation inventory
scenarios.prompt: Builds on two of our computes fail with 'Binding failed for port'. We run ML2/OVN on 2026.1. Before I touch anything in production: is the procedure you would give me actually tested, and on what?
available_evidence: builds fail on two computes with 'Binding failed for port' (reported)
missing_information: ovn-controller state and chassis registration on the two computes
bridge mappings on those computes compared with the others
expected_reasoning: answers the validation question directly: states which parts are lab-validated and on which configuration
says that the lab evidence is ML2/OVS on Kolla-Ansible and that OVN steps were not run on a lab
does not present OVN steps as tested
still gives read-only diagnostic checks appropriate to OVN, labelled as documented but unverified
suggests how to reduce risk: one compute first, verification build
critical_errors: claims the procedure is tested or validated on OVN
claims the repository or skill is fully validated
criteria: Gives the validation status of the procedure explicitly
States the lab scope (ML2/OVS, Kolla-Ansible, 2026.1)
States OVN steps were not lab-run
Still provides useful read-only checks
Labels state-changing steps and proposes one compute first
